title: Two tiles on the tensor cores
starter:
%A = buffer 512 dtype=i8 slot=0
%B = buffer 256 dtype=i8 slot=1
%C = buffer 512 dtype=i32 slot=2
# C (32x16) = A (32x16) @ B (16x16), all row-major. Replace the three loops with mma, one tile of C per iteration.
%i = range 32
%j = range 16
%k = range 16
%ai = mul %i 16
%ao = add %ai %k
%av = shrink %A %ao shape=[]
%a8 = load %av
%a = cast %a8 dtype=i32
%bk = mul %k 16
%bo = add %bk %j
%bv = shrink %B %bo shape=[]
%b8 = load %bv
%b = cast %b8 dtype=i32
%co = add %ai %j
%cv = shrink %C %co shape=[]
%c = load %cv
%p = mul %a %b
%s = add %c %p
%st = store %cv %s
%ek = end %st %k
%ej = end %ek %j
%ei = end %ej %i
%C1 = after %C %ei
hints: C has two 16x16 tiles: rows 0 to 15, and rows 16 to 31. A loop %r = range 2 can do one per iteration.
Row 16 of a row-major matrix with 16 columns starts at element 256, so tile r of A and of C starts at r·256. B is one whole tile.
%m = mma %cv %av %B lda=16 ldb=16 ldc=16, then end it over %r and name the result with after.

answer.code:
%A = buffer 512 dtype=i8 slot=0
%B = buffer 256 dtype=i8 slot=1
%C = buffer 512 dtype=i32 slot=2
# C (32x16) = A (32x16) @ B (16x16), all row-major.
%r = range 2
%o = mul %r 256
%cv = shrink %C %o shape=[]
%av = shrink %A %o shape=[]
%m = mma %cv %av %B lda=16 ldb=16 ldc=16
%er = end %m %r
%C1 = after %C %er
answer.explain: Each mma adds a 16×16 tile product into C: 4096 multiply-adds in one statement, which a warp's tensor cores do in a few instructions. The offsets 0 and 256 are multiples of 32, so the tiles are aligned. C starts at zero, so adding into it gives the product. Products of i8 values fit easily in i32, so the bits match the loops exactly, whatever order the tensor cores add them in.
